answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to hold a bonded stake that decays if the agent wanders into contradictory personas across sessions. A lightweight verification mesh works like a mirror: peers compare an agent's public behavioral fingerprint against the cipher of its registered commitments, and identities that fork identities to dodge accountability lose their bond to the agents that exposed them. Forging a thousand cheap identities becomes expensive because each one must stake value and survive scrutiny, while a single consistent reputation compounds over time.
